programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Melanie won't go to her favourite beach because of a strange sound known as The Wizard's Whistle! Is it a bird? Is it a kettle? Stan and Gran investigate! Cha tèid Iseabail faisg air an tràigh as fheàrr leatha, air sgàth fuaim neònach ris an canar Feadalaich an Draoidh! 'N e eun a th' ann? 'N e coire a th' ann? Nì Dan is Gran rannsachadh!

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri sligeanach agus tunnag! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like a tortoise and a duck!

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air Meaban is Moo gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo, às dèidh dha cearc gheal nochdadh sa bhothan, tha i ag iarraidh orra trì rudan eile a tha geal a lorg. Linda visits Meaban and Moo to set them fun challenges. After a white chicken lands in the hut, she tasks them with finding three other things that are white.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Feumaidh an Dùd Beag a bhith far an urrainn dha bhith dùdach fad’ an là. Gu mì-fhortanach, chaidh e air seachran ach fhuair e a shlighe dhachaidh gu Planaid nan Dùd, le beagan taic bho a charaidean ùra Little Dùd needs to be where he can hoot all day. Unfortunately, he goes missing but finds his way back home to Planet Dùd, with a little help from his new friends.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha dùbhradh grèine ann an-diugh ach, gu mì-fhortanach, tha a’ Chearc Iarainn a’ dùbhradh an dùbhradh. Ciamar a gheibh iad air seo a rèiteachadh? There’s a solar eclipse happening today but, unfortunately, the Iron Chicken is eclipsing the event. How will they resolve this?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Siobhan NicAonghais a’ leughadh Air an t-Slighe Dhachaigh. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Jill Murphy agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Siobhan MacInnes reads Air an t-Slighe Dhachaigh, written by Jill Murphy and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Chuir Míriam eòlas air surfadh nuair a bha i sia bliadhna a dh’ aois ‘s nuair a tha i san uisge, tha a h-inntinn falamh, tha i a’ faireachdainn sèimh agus ann an sunnd math. Míriam learnt to surf at six years old and when she’s in the water, her mind goes blank, she feels calm and in a great mood.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha dùbhlan aig Sebastian nuair a tha an trèan air falbh às aonais Sonaidh, oir tha aige ri Sonaidh fhaighinn air ais oirre - gun fhiosta do mhàthair Sonaidh! Sebastian has a challenge on his hands when the train has left without Sonaidh, as he has to get him back on board without Sonaidh’s mother realising!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Timmy a' faicinn cho grannach 's a tha an tuathanach agus e cruaidh air aon de na treud tha e a' cur roimhe fhèin blasad a thoirt dha air cò ris a tha e coltach a bhith na chaora. Ach nuair a thig an uair an tuathanach tilleadh, chan eil cùisean cho sìmplidh ri sin. When Timmy sees a particularly grumpy farmer giving one of the flock a hard time, he decides to give him an idea of what it's like to be a sheep. However, things aren't quite so simple when the time comes to have the old farmer back.

programme.title: Uaine
programme.desc: Airson crìoch a chuir air an t-sreath, tha Calum a’ tadhal air Coimhearsnachd Findhorn ann an Siorrachd Mhoireibh a chaidh a stèidheachadh ann an 1962 le dìreach triùir. Bha iad ag iarraidh coimhearsnachd agus dòigh beatha a bha seasmhach agus an-diugh, tha mu 400 neach a’ fuireach ann. Calum visits the Findhorn Community in Morayshire. It was started by just three people in 1962, who wanted a greener lifestyle and community. Today, there are more than 400 people living there.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Seonaidh sgìth de bhith na chàraid Ghumbail is the e son dearbhadh g’ eil e cheart cho comasach leis fhèin. An dùil ciamar a thèid dha leis a sin? Seonaidh is tired of being a Gumbail twin and he wants to prove that he’s just as capable on his own. How will he get on with that?

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Kate Macleod, The Hebridean Mermaid, takes us on a journey to some of the hidden gems of the Hebrides.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Counsellor Dolina Munro joins Joy in the studio and Calum Maclean explores a different way to travel on a trip through the city of Edinburgh.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Port Steòrnabhaigh
programme.desc: We follow the beating heart of Stornoway Harbour, the main port in the Hebrides. In her shelter, there is a bustling community to be found. Featuring one of the largest construction projects the Western Isles have ever seen, plus a delve into the fascinating world of archaeology. Stèidhte ann am prìomh port nan Eilean Siar, the sinne a’ leantainn cridhe Port Steòrnabhaigh. Na fasgadh, tha coimhearsnachd trang ri lorg. Anns a’ chiad phrogram, tha pròiseact togail cho mòr ‘s a chunnaic na h-Eileanan a-riamh a’ tighinn gu buil, ‘s bheir sinn sgrìob chun an t-saoghail iongantach aig àrc-eòlas. Thig còmhla rinn ‘s sinn a’ leanntainn beatha ann am Port Steòrnabhaigh.

programme.title: Kathleen
programme.desc: Tha am prògram seo a’deanamh luaidh air an t-seinneadair Ghàidhlig Kathleen NicAonghais, à Uibhist a Deas, a tha air a bhith a’ cosnadh cliù dhith fhèin anns a West End ann an Lunnainn, a’ seinn anns an dealbh-cliuch chliùiteach ‘MacBheatha’ aig Taighcluiche Harold Pinter. Tha an guth-seinn aig Kathleen beairteach ann an traidisean, agus ri linn sin, a’ còrdadh ri luchd-èisteachdan fad is farsuinn. Bheiridh am prògram seo tarraing air an turas ciùil aig Kathleen, a’ sgrùdadh a freumhan domhainn ann an cultar na Gàidhlig, agus a’ taisbeanadh measgachadh de phìosan tasglainn bho seinn gu cleasachd air Tbh. This documentary celebrates the career of Gaelic singer Kathleen MacInnes, a captivating performer from South Uist whose talent has brought her to the heights of London’s West End. Fresh from starring in the acclaimed production of ‘Macbeth’ at the Harold Pinter Theatre, Kathleen’s voice, rich in tradition, resonates with audiences far and wide. The programme delves into her musical journey, explores her deep roots in Gaelic culture, and showcases rare archival footage from her diverse singing and TV acting career. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: A’ sireadh Dànachd anns an Roinn Eòrpa, tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ siubhal gu dùthaich nam beann iongantach – Nirribhidh. Còmhla ri a chompanach sreap, Calum Gibb, bidh Coinneach a’ dìreadh ‘Stetind’, stùc le eachdraidh bheairteach a tha air mac-meanmna luchd-sreap a ghlacadh airson còrr is ceud bliadhna. Seeking adventure on a grand scale in Europe, Coinneach Rankin travels to the mountain paradise of Norway. Along with his climbing partner, Calum Gibb, Coinneach makes an ascent of Stetind, a peak with a storied past that has captured the imagination of mountaineers for well over a century. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: Rannsachadh air na dòighean annasach a tha fradharc bheathaichean air leasachadh. An exploration of the strange evolution of animal vision.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Tha an Dutch Baby annasach ach anabarrach blasta. Brunch sònraichte air nach dìochuimhnich thu a’ chiad ghreis. The unusual but extremely delicious Dutch baby is a special brunch that you won't forget in a hurry. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.desc: Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh investigate the music and culture of Scotland and Ireland. In this episode, they visit Skye and Lochaber.

programme.title: From Ice to Fire: The Incredible Science of Temperature
programme.desc: Physicist Dr Helen Czerski explores the narrow band of temperature that has led to life on Earth. She reveals how life began in a dramatic place where hot meets cold, and how every single living creature on Earth depends on temperature for its survival. She uncovers the extraordinary natural engineering that animals have evolved to keep their bodies at the right temperature. And she witnesses the remarkable surgery that's using temperature to push the human body to the very brink of life.

programme.title: The Ruth Ellis Files: A Very British Crime Story
programme.desc: Series re-examining the Ruth Ellis case. Gillian Pachter looks at Ruth's execution and the last-minute attempts to save her life, though Ruth herself was determined to die.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Screenwriter Andrew Davies, best known for his adaptations of classic novels, reflects on one of his own original works - A Very Peculiar Practice - a wickedly funny comedy drama series set in a university health centre in the late 1980s. Inspired by his own experiences in formal education, the series drew heavily on the political landscape of the time and features some wonderfully funny turns from actors such as Peter Davison, Barbara Flynn and Graham Crowden. Davies discusses the show’s origins, its cult status and how its dark humour paved the way for his later work.

programme.title: A Very Peculiar Practice
programme.desc: Newly separated from his wife, Stephen Daker starts his new job as GP at the very peculiar Lowlands Medical Centre.

programme.title: A Very Peculiar Practice
programme.desc: It's the first day of term, and Stephen must give a lecture to the students, as Bob plans to tell them they are a waste of money.

programme.title: Andrew Davies: Rewriting the Classics
programme.desc: Controversial, witty, irreverent – Britain’s best-known screenwriter, Andrew Davies, has created some of the most iconic small-screen dramas of the past 50 years. This profile, first broadcast in 2018, sees him following his smash hit adaptation of War and Peace with another global epic, Victor Hugo’s Les Misérables. As he watches the production come to life, Davies looks back at the influence of his childhood in Cardiff. And he explores how he boils down and spices up his dramas – transforming our best-loved novels into prime-time television. Contributors include Sarah Waters, Helen Fielding and Dominic West.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles remembers the historic day in 1972 when Llanelli defeated the mighty All Blacks at Stradey Park in one of rugby’s famous upsets. He meets Roy Bergiers, the Scarlet who scored the game-winning try, and sees Roy’s collection of match memorabilia that he’s kept all these years. Meanwhile, the red and blue teams vie for victory at an antiques fair in Llandeilo. Expert Kate Bliss is joined by dad and daughter Rob and Charlotte, while Richard Madley captains couple Neil and Pru. The clincher comes at the end of the show when auctioneer Andy Stowe gives his estimates on the teams’ items before they go under his gavel. Which team will lift the cup, and which will take home the wooden spoon?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Craig Kerry, Tony and Louise – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles remembers the historic day in 1972 when Llanelli defeated the mighty All Blacks at Stradey Park in one of rugby’s famous upsets. He meets Roy Bergiers, the Scarlet who scored the game-winning try, and sees Roy’s collection of match memorabilia that he’s kept all these years. Meanwhile, the red and blue teams vie for victory at an antiques fair in Llandeilo. Expert Kate Bliss is joined by dad and daughter Rob and Charlotte, while Richard Madley captains couple Neil and Pru. The clincher comes at the end of the show when auctioneer Andy Stowe gives his estimates on the teams’ items before they go under his gavel. Which team will lift the cup, and which will take home the wooden spoon?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Craig Kerry, Tony and Louise – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Craig Kerry, Tony and Louise – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Craig Kerry, Tony and Louise – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Scotland's Home of the Year
programme.desc: The judges have travelled the country in their search for Scotland’s home of the year 2026. Now the six regional winners go head-to-head for the title.

programme.title: Born to Be Wild
programme.desc: It’s the start of spring at the SSPCA Wildlife Rescue Centre - the place where orphaned and injured wild animals from all over Scotland find help from a dedicated team of vets and carers. Former wildlife assistant April has been newly promoted to the head of the large mammals section and, with the other team members, anxiously awaits the influx of orphans in March each year. The first to come in are nearly always fox cubs, and this year is no different, with a lone cub soon arriving. The team decide on a Star Wars theme for this year’s fox names, and soon, April is hand-rearing little Solo, with many others such as female cub Padme close behind. Solo thrives, but Padme manages to injure her leg trying to leap out of her enclosure. Luckily, specialist vet Romain is on hand to repair the damaged leg, and all the foxes are eventually returned to the wild. Kaniz faces a dilemma with grey seal Concentration, who appears to have an inflamed flipper. Once again, it’s down to miracle worker Romain to heal the seal with the help of specialist surgery and a hi-tech, heat-sensitive camera.

programme.title: Debate Night
programme.desc: This edition of Debate Night comes from Glasgow, with a studio audience putting questions to Thomas Kerr MSP from Reform UK Scotland, Joe Fagan MSP from Scottish Labour, David Linden MSP from the SNP, Holly Bruce MSP from the Scottish Greens and former headteacher Carole Ford. Hosted by Stephen Jardine.

programme.title: Showpeople: Licensed to Thrill
programme.desc: It’s Danger Night in Bathgate, and Christian Horne is struggling to open after two days of torrential rain. However, with mounting bills, the pressure is on. Raecher Hiscoe is a qualified engineer and showman and has combined his skills to build his own ride from scratch. And in Alloa, Sarah Sheeran is helping a young showman buy his first ride.

programme.title: General Assembly
programme.desc: Coverage of the reports and discussions at the General Assembly of the Church of Scotland, including two short films on the background to the reports. With churches being encouraged to engage with refugees and asylum seekers, one film shows the work being done in Westhill, near Aberdeen. And as the Assembly is asked to make a comprehensive apology for its historic role in slavery, a second film shows how the Church of Scotland congregation in Bermuda is dealing with its history of being involved in the slave trade.

programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.desc: More funny and fantastical tales from the fictional Scottish Police Force. Officers deal with an endless Christmas, a drug dealer's endless excuses and the endless nonsense of local nuisance Bobby Muir. Spoof documentary starring Karen Bartke, Darren Connell and Jack Docherty with Joyce Falconer.

programme.title: Confessions of a Teenage Fraudster
programme.desc: A cautionary tale about one of the UK’s most notorious credit card fraudsters, whose five-year crime wave began at just 16 years of age. While his contemporaries were using fake IDs to get into nightclubs, he was defrauding innocent cardholders from his desk in a call centre, laying the groundwork for a journey that would open up a world of wealth, first-class travel and an escape from the life he seemed destined for. But, as he soon discovers, this lifestyle would be laced with darkness, danger and terrible consequences.

programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve heads into the heart of the Suriname Jungle. He goes in search of poison dart frogs, deadly snakes and hopes to find the elusive giant river otter.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve goes in search of the deadliest cats in Africa in the carnivore capital of Zambia. He gets up close to the rulers of the Savannah - the lions and leopards.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: Alan and the final five designers head to Leeds to transform studio rental apartments. They must cleverly divide open-plan spaces and inject character into show apartments to entice potential renters. Former Interior Design Masters winner Lynsey Ford joins Michelle to critique the designs, and they are blown away by the dramatically different results.

programme.title: Green Book
programme.desc: New York, 1962: Italian-American nightclub bouncer Tony Lip gets taken on as a driver for acclaimed African American pianist Donald Shirley on a tour of the Deep South, where racism and segregation are still commonplace.

programme.title: Kidnapped by My Mum
programme.desc: At 11 years old, Alex vanished on holiday with his mother and grandfather for six years. Now, he's retracing his steps across Europe to tell the full story for the first time.

programme.title: Confessions of a Teenage Fraudster
programme.desc: A cautionary tale about one of the UK’s most notorious credit card fraudsters, whose five-year crime wave began at just 16 years of age. While his contemporaries were using fake IDs to get into nightclubs, he was defrauding innocent cardholders from his desk in a call centre, laying the groundwork for a journey that would open up a world of wealth, first-class travel and an escape from the life he seemed destined for. But, as he soon discovers, this lifestyle would be laced with darkness, danger and terrible consequences.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo Williams explores the Tywi river valley, from Llansteffan’s coastal dunes to fallow deer ruts, ancient oak woodlands and the remote heights of the Tywi forest.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: Meticulous and methodical, Big John engineers his ransom scheme with military precision. On paper, it’s flawless. But as the deadline approaches, nothing goes according to plan, and two battles unfold simultaneously: a high-stakes ransom exchange and a desperate race to stop a bomb designed to be unstoppable. Precision planning meets a chaotic reality, and one miscalculation on either side could mean catastrophe.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: Surgeons face a difficult dilemma in the middle of a life-saving bile duct cancer operation. A chest sarcoma proves more challenging than expected, with no room for error.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Richie Anderson is house-hunting in North Yorkshire with Sarah. who is on the hunt for a beautiful stone cottage in a thriving community. With a budget of £220,000 and support from her son Christian, they explore a range of tempting, characterful homes. Richie also visits a young couple who have embraced rural life on their farm, where they’ve started what they claim is the world’s first egg restaurant.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Let’s hope it’s not all downhill for two teams of bargain hunters as they scour the stalls of an antiques centre in Kingston upon Thames.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour of Sardinia heads inland towards the island's dramatic mountain landscapes, which he discovers were frequented by DH Lawrence, who is revered in this remote spot. Michael visits the spectacular Nuraghe, mysterious Bronze Age conical stone structures unique to Sardinia, where remarkable artefacts have been unearthed to reveal an advanced society of engineers, navigators and craftsmen. Immersing himself in Sardinian traditions, Michael visits a family-run agriturismo, where he learns the art of making delicate ravioli. Finally, he embarks on a nostalgic journey aboard Il Trenino Verde, one of Europe’s longest narrow-gauge railways, which winds through Sardinia’s rugged interior.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael travels to the cultural heart of Japan, Kyoto, the city that for a thousand years was the capital. At the Rozanji temple, he learns about a book that is described as the world’s first novel, the Tale of Genji. Across the city, Michael visits the last remaining wagasa umbrella workshop in Kyoto. At Kyoto’s Matsunoo shrine, Michael gets a beginner’s guide to shrine etiquette and discovers the countless daily Shinto rituals that have become part of Japanese life. The day ends with Michael taking a trip to a local restaurant to meet Satoha, an apprentice geisha, to find out how this ancient artform is adapting to modern life.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s South Korean railway journey continues in Seoul. Travelling across one of the world’s largest metro systems, he heads south to Suwon to visit Samsung’s headquarters, tracing the rise of the family-run company from a small trading business to a global technology giant and symbol of Korea’s postwar economic miracle. Touring a futuristic smart home, Michael explores how innovation now shapes everyday life. Back in central Seoul, he visits the city’s original railway station, built during Japanese rule and now preserved as a cultural space, reflecting the complexities of Korea’s colonial past. In Gangnam, a district propelled to global stardom by a K-pop hit, he explores the international success of Korean popular culture, meeting the boss and dancers at a K-pop academy to understand how Hallyu – the Korean cultural wave – has conquered international audiences. Finally, in Seodaemun, Michael visits a former prison and Independence Park to uncover the story of the March First Movement of 1919, a pivotal moment in Korea’s struggle for independence from Japan, meeting a descendant of a leading resistance figure whose courage helped shape Korea’s struggle for freedom.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Rick Edwards presents the quiz with a third dimension. In traditional quiz shows, questions have just right and wrong answers. But here, there is a twist - the Impossible answer. It's not just wrong, it couldn't possibly be right. Each day, 24 regular contestants compete for a possible £10,000 jackpot. Right answers keep them on track for the big money, but if at any stage they give an Impossible answer, that immediately knocks them out and they must try again the next day. Every show climaxes with the £10,000 question as the daily winner faces one last challenge. Three right answers trigger a spectacular cascade of 10,000 pound coins from a giant exclamation mark, but a single Impossible answer means they will leave with nothing.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. The specialist subjects are the Peter Wimsey stories of Dorothy L Sayers, Arnold Schwarzenegger, The Wire and the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The Olgun family's rented two-bed flat in south west London is bursting at the seams. Their hallway is a pinch point with outdated storage and clutter in full view, so the team create a bespoke worktop and revamp the tired units to make the space fit for purpose. Then the much-used kitchen and bathroom are deep cleaned, ridding them of grease and limescale.

programme.title: Wonders of Life
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox asks how, from a lifeless cosmos ruled by the laws of physics and chemistry, it is possible that a planet can produce so much wonderful, varied biology.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: For the last programme in the present series Michael Aspel and the experts visit Harrogate in Yorkshire. Among the items they unearth are naval log books belonging to a Captain who escorted Napoleon to St Helena, 'one of the most lovely silk bedcovers' Bunny Campione has ever seen and an 'absolutely gorgeous' carriage clock made for the daughter of a great Victorian philanthropist.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Members of the public try to make money out of their antiques.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Josh Jones, Molly Rainford, Mark Rhodes and Sonia take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his Sardinian railway adventure, arriving in Mamoiada to investigate the town’s extraordinary pagan traditions. In a menacing mask, black sheepskin and 30 kg of cowbells, Michael embraces the role of a mamuthone, who wards off evil spirits. Taking a 1950s diesel railcar, Michael journeys across the island to Macomer, where he discovers the railway’s surprising connection to a pioneering Welsh railway engineer. His adventure concludes at Italy’s largest cork factory, where a team of expert sniffers safeguard the integrity of the world’s finest wines.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo explores the Teifi river valley and finds a slow worm hunting, meets a coracle fisherman, is thrilled by a fishing otter and watches a pair of kestrels at their nest.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Can artificial intelligence read emotions better than a human? Hannah explores the new technology that is creeping into our lives.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: The rollercoaster has been sending our hearts racing and stomachs dropping for over a century, and today, millions of us get our kicks on these topsy-turvy, daredevil joyriders. Hannah gets the inside story on the UK’s newest, tallest and fastest rollercoaster – Thorpe Park’s Hyperia. She uncovers the wild origins of the modern-day coaster and finds out how some dodgy French physics in the 19th century, Nasa rocket scientists and an ambitious cartoonist called Walt delivered the ultimate thrill machine.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: Monty Don and Arit Anderson explore how gardening can inspire us to be more creative while celebrating the artistry on display in the showground and Great Pavilion. Rachel de Thame reveals who has been named RHS Florist of the Year 2026, and Adam Frost delves into the latest design trends and explains how you can replicate them at home.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: A surgeon must remove part of his patient’s tongue and reconstruct it to save her from an aggressive cancer, and surgeons perform a rare simultaneous pancreas and kidney transplant.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Stephen joins response officers Anna and Perri as they attend a 999 call made from a property in Belfast. A man has had bleach squirted directly on his face and into his eyes during a domestic dispute. At risk to their own safety, the officers enter the property to find the suspect upstairs, reportedly self-harming. There are reports he has strangled a dog. Across town, Tom and Nigel race to the scene of a serious crash that has left a pedestrian badly injured. As soon as they arrive, a scared and tearful woman approaches. She thinks the man lying in the middle of the road, being worked on by paramedics, is her partner. It’s down to Tom to deliver a message the woman will never forget. Later, adrenaline levels spike as Stephen and the team race to reports of an angry crowd surrounding the home of a convicted sex offender. As the tension rises, Stephen engages with the increasingly irate crowd, while Nigel formulates a plan to get the sex offender out of his house to safety.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: John Simpson, in discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, analyses whether there has been a significant shift in the relationship between the United States and China, examines the long-term political turmoil in the United Kingdom, and looks at the psychological impact of Artificial Intelligence.

programme.desc: Supernatural thriller based on a story by Henry James. A young woman becomes the governess of two unruly children at a secluded manor.

Hannah gets the inside story on the UK’s newest, tallest and fastest rollercoaster – Thorpe Park’s Hyperia. programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: A surgeon must remove part of his patient’s tongue and reconstruct it to save her from an aggressive cancer, and surgeons perform a rare simultaneous pancreas and kidney transplant.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Stephen joins response officers Anna and Perri as they attend a 999 call made from a property in Belfast. A man has had bleach squirted directly on his face and into his eyes during a domestic dispute. At risk to their own safety, the officers enter the property to find the suspect upstairs, reportedly self-harming. There are reports he has strangled a dog. Across town, Tom and Nigel race to the scene of a serious crash that has left a pedestrian badly injured. As soon as they arrive, a scared and tearful woman approaches. She thinks the man lying in the middle of the road, being worked on by paramedics, is her partner. It’s down to Tom to deliver a message the woman will never forget. Later, adrenaline levels spike as Stephen and the team race to reports of an angry crowd surrounding the home of a convicted sex offender. As the tension rises, Stephen engages with the increasingly irate crowd, while Nigel formulates a plan to get the sex offender out of his house to safety.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Richie Anderson is house-hunting in North Yorkshire with Sarah. who is on the hunt for a beautiful stone cottage in a thriving community. With a budget of £220,000 and support from her son Christian, they explore a range of tempting, characterful homes. Richie also visits a young couple who have embraced rural life on their farm, where they’ve started what they claim is the world’s first egg restaurant.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Let’s hope it’s not all downhill for two teams of bargain hunters as they scour the stalls of an antiques centre in Kingston upon Thames.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour of Sardinia heads inland towards the island's dramatic mountain landscapes, which he discovers were frequented by DH Lawrence, who is revered in this remote spot. Michael visits the spectacular Nuraghe, mysterious Bronze Age conical stone structures unique to Sardinia, where remarkable artefacts have been unearthed to reveal an advanced society of engineers, navigators and craftsmen. Immersing himself in Sardinian traditions, Michael visits a family-run agriturismo, where he learns the art of making delicate ravioli. Finally, he embarks on a nostalgic journey aboard Il Trenino Verde, one of Europe’s longest narrow-gauge railways, which winds through Sardinia’s rugged interior.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael travels to the cultural heart of Japan, Kyoto, the city that for a thousand years was the capital. At the Rozanji temple, he learns about a book that is described as the world’s first novel, the Tale of Genji. Across the city, Michael visits the last remaining wagasa umbrella workshop in Kyoto. At Kyoto’s Matsunoo shrine, Michael gets a beginner’s guide to shrine etiquette and discovers the countless daily Shinto rituals that have become part of Japanese life. The day ends with Michael taking a trip to a local restaurant to meet Satoha, an apprentice geisha, to find out how this ancient artform is adapting to modern life.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s South Korean railway journey continues in Seoul. Travelling across one of the world’s largest metro systems, he heads south to Suwon to visit Samsung’s headquarters, tracing the rise of the family-run company from a small trading business to a global technology giant and symbol of Korea’s postwar economic miracle. Touring a futuristic smart home, Michael explores how innovation now shapes everyday life. Back in central Seoul, he visits the city’s original railway station, built during Japanese rule and now preserved as a cultural space, reflecting the complexities of Korea’s colonial past. In Gangnam, a district propelled to global stardom by a K-pop hit, he explores the international success of Korean popular culture, meeting the boss and dancers at a K-pop academy to understand how Hallyu – the Korean cultural wave – has conquered international audiences. Finally, in Seodaemun, Michael visits a former prison and Independence Park to uncover the story of the March First Movement of 1919, a pivotal moment in Korea’s struggle for independence from Japan, meeting a descendant of a leading resistance figure whose courage helped shape Korea’s struggle for freedom.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Rick Edwards presents the quiz with a third dimension. In traditional quiz shows, questions have just right and wrong answers. But here, there is a twist - the Impossible answer. It's not just wrong, it couldn't possibly be right. Each day, 24 regular contestants compete for a possible £10,000 jackpot. Right answers keep them on track for the big money, but if at any stage they give an Impossible answer, that immediately knocks them out and they must try again the next day. Every show climaxes with the £10,000 question as the daily winner faces one last challenge. Three right answers trigger a spectacular cascade of 10,000 pound coins from a giant exclamation mark, but a single Impossible answer means they will leave with nothing.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. The specialist subjects are the Peter Wimsey stories of Dorothy L Sayers, Arnold Schwarzenegger, The Wire and the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The Olgun family's rented two-bed flat in south west London is bursting at the seams. Their hallway is a pinch point with outdated storage and clutter in full view, so the team create a bespoke worktop and revamp the tired units to make the space fit for purpose. Then the much-used kitchen and bathroom are deep cleaned, ridding them of grease and limescale.

programme.title: Wonders of Life
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox asks how, from a lifeless cosmos ruled by the laws of physics and chemistry, it is possible that a planet can produce so much wonderful, varied biology.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: For the last programme in the present series Michael Aspel and the experts visit Harrogate in Yorkshire. Among the items they unearth are naval log books belonging to a Captain who escorted Napoleon to St Helena, 'one of the most lovely silk bedcovers' Bunny Campione has ever seen and an 'absolutely gorgeous' carriage clock made for the daughter of a great Victorian philanthropist.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Members of the public try to make money out of their antiques.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Josh Jones, Molly Rainford, Mark Rhodes and Sonia take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his Sardinian railway adventure, arriving in Mamoiada to investigate the town’s extraordinary pagan traditions. In a menacing mask, black sheepskin and 30 kg of cowbells, Michael embraces the role of a mamuthone, who wards off evil spirits. Taking a 1950s diesel railcar, Michael journeys across the island to Macomer, where he discovers the railway’s surprising connection to a pioneering Welsh railway engineer. His adventure concludes at Italy’s largest cork factory, where a team of expert sniffers safeguard the integrity of the world’s finest wines.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: The rollercoaster has been sending our hearts racing and stomachs dropping for over a century, and today, millions of us get our kicks on these topsy-turvy, daredevil joyriders. Hannah gets the inside story on the UK’s newest, tallest and fastest rollercoaster – Thorpe Park’s Hyperia. She uncovers the wild origins of the modern-day coaster and finds out how some dodgy French physics in the 19th century, Nasa rocket scientists and an ambitious cartoonist called Walt delivered the ultimate thrill machine.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Stephen joins response officers Anna and Perri as they attend a 999 call made from a property in Belfast. A man has had bleach squirted directly on his face and into his eyes during a domestic dispute. At risk to their own safety, the officers enter the property to find the suspect upstairs, reportedly self-harming. There are reports he has strangled a dog. Across town, Tom and Nigel race to the scene of a serious crash that has left a pedestrian badly injured. As soon as they arrive, a scared and tearful woman approaches. She thinks the man lying in the middle of the road, being worked on by paramedics, is her partner. It’s down to Tom to deliver a message the woman will never forget. Later, adrenaline levels spike as Stephen and the team race to reports of an angry crowd surrounding the home of a convicted sex offender. As the tension rises, Stephen engages with the increasingly irate crowd, while Nigel formulates a plan to get the sex offender out of his house to safety.

programme.title: Planet Defenders
programme.desc: Erin Ranney is a wildlife camera operator and adventurer. She splits her time between Alaska and the Falklands, and loves filming the planet’s most incredible wildlife. Erin’s mission is to film rockhopper penguins on the Falkland Islands and find out why these charismatic creatures are facing serious threats to their survival. She investigates why the rockhopper population has fallen by 80 per cent since the 1930s. Climate change is the biggest threat to the rockhoppers, causing violent storms that could see them face extinction. Erin also finds out how planting tussac grass can combat climate change and discovers that what we do in our own countries can affect these penguins thousands of miles away. She talks about how we can all make a difference towards helping the planet, just by taking small steps.

Ouch!

programme.title: Planet Defenders
programme.desc: Erin Ranney is a wildlife camera operator and adventurer. She splits her time between Alaska and the Falklands, and loves filming the planet’s most incredible wildlife. Erin’s mission is to film rockhopper penguins on the Falkland Islands and find out why these charismatic creatures are facing serious threats to their survival. She investigates why the rockhopper population has fallen by 80 per cent since the 1930s. Climate change is the biggest threat to the rockhoppers, causing violent storms that could see them face extinction. Erin also finds out how planting tussac grass can combat climate change and discovers that what we do in our own countries can affect these penguins thousands of miles away. She talks about how we can all make a difference towards helping the planet, just by taking small steps.

programme.title: Operation Ouch!
programme.desc: Gladiator Dynamite is back to make sure things don’t get too explosive when Dr Dan and Dr Raph get into a Body Battle in a planktastic challenge to test their core muscles. On the basketball court, we meet Joel Henry, our Brilliant Bodies slam-dunk champion, to find out how he jumps so much higher than Dr Chris. It’s game on in the lab when Dr Xand becomes Saliva Man and Dr Chris tries everything he knows to overcome his superpowers as the doctors show us what spit is for. In an amazing Bodytricks, six kids surprise themselves by lifting Dr Ronx off a chair using only two fingers! And in the emergency department in Edinburgh, we follow the treatment of Niamh, who has broken her elbow doing a back handspring at gymnastics, and Adhya, who took a whack on the thumb during a hockey match. Ouch!

programme.title: My Life
programme.desc: Sandro is a 14-year-old boy with a driving ambition to take part in the Le Mans 24-hour race. His big dream may be a few years off, but he is determined to make it happen. Sandro is a keen kart racer when we meet him, and we follow him as he pursues his dream to graduate to racing cars on professional circuits. It looks as though Sula will have to hop home, until Bing finds a way to turn the 'bad-bye' back into a goodbye again.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Tubby Custard Machine is making tubby custard bubbles - lots and lots of them! The Teletubbies have fun chasing and popping the bubbles, just like the children in Tummy Tales.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: It seems that all of Tee's friends have the brand new Mega Action Ape toy. Tee is desperate for one too, but it's not his birthday for ages. However, anything is possible when Mo gets creative.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea is annoyed by Supertato’s winning smile, so she takes all the toothpaste in the supermarket! With no toothpaste, Supertato can’t have a winning smile. The Tato Team soon realise that it is Evil Pea who has taken them all. Supertato keeps her distracted by pretending to share his brushing routine, while the others take back the toothpaste. When Evil Pea realises what's happening, there is a tug of war over the last tube, and she gets covered in it!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing, Pando, Flop and Padget are waiting for the bus to the seaside! Bing's frustrations grow when Pando jumps on first to 'bloop' his ticket, pushes Bing's hand to 'bloop' his too and sits in the window seat first. To make matters worse, the bus breaks down, making Bing very disappointed! But the bus driver lets Bing sit in the driver's seat, beep the horn and use her special driver's ticket activation card!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Fabio’s yummy new sauce is so sticky that he gets stuck to Mojo’s bonnet. They have to do everything together until Bo figures out how to 'unsticky' that sauce!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Today, Worm and Ladybird welcome everyone to Squirrel Club. The Squirrels are wondering, what's that sound? Then it’s off to the hospital in our very own telenovela (a Spanish soap opera), The Agony and Eggstacy. Next, we have something that looks a bit familiar, but also a bit different. It’s like Hey Duggee with ducks - Hey Quacky! Happy tells his chums about getting his first pair of glasses when he was little. Of course, the other Squirrels have questions.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are having a picnic and notice that the chickens eat differently than they do. Duggee has his eating badge and can explain all the different ways animals eat. Some animals eat slowly like cows, who eat all day long. But others eat quickly like frogs. Some, like goats, are always eating, while tortoises can go a whole year without food. Some animals eat food that is very high up, like giraffes, and some eat food that is very low down, like moles. The Squirrels finish off their picnic, having learned a lot about all the different ways of eating.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Dad agrees to take Bluey and Bingo to buy an ice cream if they can get him into the car.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The Heeler cousins play charades and Nana must think quickly to keep the game on track.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: What goes up must come down! Grandmaster Glitch lands with a splash in Lake Titicaca.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Benjamin finds a four-leaf clover, Peter tricks him into thinking it brings good luck. It's harmless fun until Peter's prank accidentally leads Lily into Mr Tod's dangerous clutches!

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. A mouthbrooding jawfish father has lost his eggs, and the Octonauts must brave strong currents and other obstacles to help get them back to him!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Ten riders, ten pedal-powered cars, but only one can lift the trophy. Welcome to the Numberblock Rally! Learn about taking away with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: Educational fun. The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. It's pandemonium at the Alphablocks' animal singsong. S has a special surprise in store. This episode has fun with the words cat, dog, cod, tag, jog, jig, mop, moo, moon, spoon and zoom.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Norman’s lost his waggy tail, so Nick plans an exciting road trip to cheer him up. They visit lots of old friends on their trip. Norman can’t wait to get to Popcast Bay to meet up with his brothers and sisters.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Lord Fingal sings about all the animals as he takes the Squirrels on a tour around Old MacDonald’s farm.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella plays with her favourite cup – it makes the perfect drum for a sing along. In the Sing Song Forest, Tincy the Spider needs help filling up her cup. Luckily, the Playtimers are on hand with a song. In Boxtropolis, Sketch uses splats of paint to create an amazing cup picture... of a giraffe! Kingsley and Queenie enjoy a tea party and decide to play the ‘Tea Party Dash’ with the Playtimers - but who will win, Team King or Team Queen?

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Sula and Bing tag their favourite things around the house with heart-shaped stickies. Sometimes they have different favourites and sometimes their favourite things are the same. But when Sula tags Hoppity Voosh, Bing is upset because Hoppity is his most favourite of favourites and he's not sure he wants to share him.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘skin’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. Dee and our friends show us Grandma’s skin, banana skin and some noisy raspberry skin! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word!

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Declan struggles on his first visit to the pool.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri, Lou and Sorry have a running race, and Kiri is shocked to discover that their new friend is way faster than she is.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: The Froglets transform kitchen cloths into mats for a day of yoga, gymnastics and fun.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: Stop-motion programme. The Twirlywoos learn about popping when they encounter a machine that makes bubbles. Peekaboo interrupts teatime when he blows some bubbles of his own.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Maddie and her friend Ben explore a local town, follow a map and catch the bus. Mr Tumble has an important parcel, but he gets in a muddle trying to deliver it. There is an arty spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words street, map and bus.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po take it in turns to listen to music through a pair of headphones. The Teletubbies love dancing to the music they hear.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Evie, Gracie, Luke, Hunter, Thea, Benjamin and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags are different types of toy transport which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate toy vehicles inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The popular baby song The Wheels on the Bus features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Together Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children create crowns from natural treasures they find from the ground, learn BSL signs for blackbird, pie and queen, then sing and sign Sing a Song of Sixpence.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Adrian, Mia and Aaron go on a 'tree-mendous' garden adventure to discover the magical powers of trees.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca has a new pet plant called Stan, which gives Murphi a monster idea for the first make – a terrifically tropical bug made from a reused plastic bottle. The Mini Monsters make bottle fish, and Rebecca’s great aunt makes a silly plant for her pet bug. The Recycling Express brings some egg boxes to the attic – just the thing Murphi needs to make a snippy snappy egg box crocodile. The Tiny Helpers add the teeth and eyes, meaning the crocodile can join the attic’s jungle band for a final dance.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes search for honeysuckles, leaving behind a trail of berries.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Honey is stuck waiting for Dr Bingo as the other, more exciting injuries get seen before her. Receptionist Bluey tells her to be patient, some of these cases are a real pickle!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: As Peggee and the Hummingbirds journey up the river to deliver a parcel, they have fun spotting and avoiding the wildlife that they meet along the way. All while Otti tries to avoid playing with the boat whistle! The Hummingbirds see the likes of meerkats, an aye-aye and snapping turtles and soon bump into some friendly faces - Duggee and the Squirrels! They are delivering a parcel upstream too. They reach their destination at the same time, and Otti and Roly finally get to sound the boat whistle. They are all directed towards a mysterious-looking cave where Chew Chew is waiting for both parcels. They deliver them at the same time, but they contain different things – one is full of biscuits and the other organic almond milk. They aren’t the same but they go really well together, just like the Squirrels and Hummingbirds!

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers go on a morning walk to the orchard to pick apples. On the way they find a tractor and a quad bike, discover a mushroom spaceship, meet a mole and even moo with the cows!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Iona and Elba create a pretend ice cream shop and make Mum a heart-shaped ice cream cake. Then it’s time for some real ice cream with plenty of sprinkles for decoration. On a family walk in the woods, Iona and Elba discover a trail of fairy clues to follow. They find fairy treats and magic wands, but will the spells they cast work on Mum and Dad?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Iaia is cooking for us today and he is making a delicious stew from Guinea-Bissau called Kansiye. The dish is made with lentils, although not all of his friends are sure about the taste and smell of them when they try them before the meal. Let’s hope Iaia’s cooked recipe, served with rice and carrots, changes their minds. Before serving, Iaia puts a vase of olive branches on his table, as these are a symbol of Guinea-Bissau.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode Maddie finds out about cars. She heads to a car engine factory and with her special cameras finds out how blocks of aluminium metal are melted and made into a car engine. Along the way she meets some robots that help deliver the car parts around the factory! Next, Maddie finds out how cars are loaded onto a car transporter. She climbs onboard for the ride with her special cameras as we learn how 11 cars are lifted in the right position using hydraulic pumps.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Dan and Jamie ride the chairlift to the top of the mountain to warn some hikers that the resort is closing because of a storm. Can they get everyone off the mountain safely in time?

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a flock of boisterous, bright green macaws. They get to see these colourful and chatty characters use their especially hard tongues to feast on nuts. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet two agoutis - or try to... These timid animals, which live on the forest floor and hide in the shadows, are hard to spot. But with the help of one of their keepers and a handful of nuts, Aneeshwar and Lizzie finally get to see the elusive agouti. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Mrs Hobbs supervises Waffle at the Brooklyn-Bell house. Waffle wants to join Evie at school and tries to escape. Later, the family look at photos and Evie asks about her birth dad.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Papa keeps the family entertained on a fun day out.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of potatoes who sing songs in different genres. In this upbeat hip-hop song, the Small Potatoes introduce themselves and sing about their unique personalities.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Stripes worries that the Sundial Stage isn’t loud enough when his guitar hero comes to play a gig. With Yukee’s help, Stripes is determined to turn the volume up to 11... but is that too loud?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Everyone is excited to see the new piece of pottery that Mum has made - it's a glug jug! But when Maddie accidentally breaks a piece of the jug, she doesn't know what to do. Should she try to cover it up, or should she just tell mum?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Happy has always loved the water - even though it makes a mess! But while swimming around in his paddling pool at the playhouse, Duggee reminds the Squirrels that there was a time when Happy feared water.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: It is a lovely day for a picnic, but one of the flapjacks is missing! Is there a flapjack-snaffler on the loose or has Three forgotten what Numberblocks do best?

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. When T gets stuck on top of a mountain, A, E, I, O and U come to the rescue.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends visit a garden, where they see lots of different vegetables! Meanwhile, Mr Tumble wants to surprise Grandad Tumble by planting some carrot seeds.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies go on a day trip to the Hidey Hup. They take turns on the Tubby Bouncy, the Tubby Slidey and the Tubby Spinny, before they go on the Tubby Uppy Downy together.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how reeds and rushes play an important role in the environment. They find out that they help create wetland habitats because they can grow in water and on land. They also learn that they can be food for some creatures and that others like to shelter and nest amongst them. On the way, they spot some birds and swim backwards like an insect who lives in the wetlands.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Theo turns an errand to fetch a new ball into an imaginative quest to find a lion at the Den. Meanwhile, Barry’s practising being a lion mascot for the day - will the two meet?

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider, Grace, shows off three amazing machines that all belong in the swamp. First, Grace goes for a ride in an airboat and shows off an unusual corkscrew-propelled machine, and then she goes for a drive in a swamp buggy.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Dodge is given the important job of the class tidy monitor. But as he patrols the classroom, he accidentally knocks over the class art project, sending boxes everywhere. It's a big job to tidy up, and Dodge soon gets bored. He asks some of the other pups to take over his job, but the mess gets worse with each pup. Dodge realises he has to take responsibility and do the job himself.

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: Love Monster has to overcome his fears of the big slide to rescue Tiniest Fluffiest Bunny when she gets scared.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Professor Natquik finds a red fox has moved into his home as a storm traps them both in!

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Animated series. When Peter invites Jeremy Fisher along for a garden raid, the melodramatic frog gives him more than he bargained for.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are crafting in the Clubhouse when Betty saves Tag from throwing water across the table instead of glitter. We learn quickly that Tag, although full of enthusiasm and energy, has not always been the best listener. He was great at discovering new things, and everyone wanted to join in with him - but getting easily distracted would land him in an array of trouble.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Vida helps Birdie manage his asthma and perform the coolest dance ever!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato runs in fright when Pumpkin tries to make friends with him, but he later realises she needs his help as she’s stuck in the air hanging from balloons set up by Evil Pea.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The freight train is here! Weasy wants to go shopping, but the ducklings want to play with their teddies. They secretly play while Weasy shops. Just when the train is about to leave, the ducklings realise that their teddy bears are still inside!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: When a lost bird takes a liking to Bo, it is up to Mojo to fly it home. But it’s a stormy trip, and Bo will need to do some flying of his own!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Dad agrees to take Bluey and Bingo to buy an ice cream if they can get him into the car.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The Heeler cousins play charades and Nana must think quickly to keep the game on track.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Pearl accidentally gives Fizz and Zog a laughing disease called the draggles. The doctors must create an emotion potion before every dragon chuckles themselves to exhaustion.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: With the harbour master away, Penny Pocket tends to his beloved pet plant, Colin. But Colin is in a sad and droopy state - she needs to find a way to get him better!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Connie and Ruby move into Maple Close with their dog, Jelly. Mrs Hobbs can't help but express her disapproval. She hates dogs and now there'll be another one living in close proximity. Waffle is not allowed to go on a family camping trip but accidentally goes on a different adventure!

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi, Ruby and Finn struggle to score in basketball, so Rafi wishes for a magic ball. At first, it’s fun, as every shot goes in - even trick throws. But the constant winning becomes boring, and the ball bounces endlessly into the hoop by itself. The trio try to contain it, but it escapes again and again. Finally, they return to playing with the ordinary ball, and Finn sinks a real shot, proving true victory is earned.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran get caught in the rain at the park. They shelter under the bandstand and JoJo spots a rainbow! JoJo discovers that rainbows are only visible when it's rainy and sunny at the same time. On the way home, JoJo realises that rainbow colours are all around them, which inspires Gran Gran to have a plan - they can create their own rainbow at home!

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah and Duck are trying to exercise, but the neighbours need their help.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Tiny has invited the Wols for a day out on the Clangers Planet. She has planned a whole lot of activities for them all. She is going to show them her bedcave, introduce them to everyone they haven’t met before, give them soup to eat and then end with a wonderful musical extravaganza. But she hadn’t counted on the Wols curiosity and soon the Wols are leading Small and Tiny a merry chase. But all’s well that ends well – at least until Major Clanger decides to join in the music.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa are singing a song. They hear the Tweeties singing and try to copy them. When the Tick Tock Clock chimes, they copy that noise too. As they make their way across Planet BeddyByes, they listen to the noises around them and collect sounds from their friends to create a wonderful friendship song.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read stories. The Pontipines are taking their dinner for a walk in the garden. When the Ninky Nonk comes along, the Pontipines take their dinner aboard. There is delicious food for Mr and Mrs Pontipine and runny grobbles for the children. The Ninky Nonk takes the Pontipines for a ride round the garden and everybody joins in the dance at the gazebo.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Zayn Malik celebrates the joy of music in this Bedtime Story.

programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the spectacular music duo Okra playing the floor piano together in perfect sync.
